A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same METAL chart-generation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–C support comparison; the appendix text is identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChartMIMIC experiments, component ablations, scaling and difficulty analyses, a modular-system comparison, and a chart-refinement case study.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–2, Figures 3–5, and the accompanying analyses.

M1.justification: The four agents, heuristic verifier, and iterative refinement procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 clarifies the existing procedure; v1 already describes threshold-based stopping and an iteration limit. The corrected stopping equation does not establish an underlying implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate chart-to-code replication on ChartMIMIC and retain the same difficulty groups and case study. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Direct Prompting, Hint-Enhanced Prompting, and Best-of-N for both Llama 3.2-11B and GPT-4o. The ablated variants and modular-system comparator are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The four F1 metrics, base models, five-iteration main setting, and 50-example modular-system comparison remain unchanged. Replacing 512–8192 tokens with 2^9–2^13 is equivalent notation, not a budget change.

E4.justification: Both retain the visual-only, code-only, and unified-critique ablations, scaling and difficulty analyses, agentic-versus-modular comparison, and refinement case study. Revised ablation averages change results, not the questions or experimental comparisons.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains its error bars without additional explanation of their statistical meaning. No repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Llama METAL's layout score from 68.10% to 58.69% and GPT-4o Best-of-N's average from 81.70% to 82.32%. Table 2 revises the V/C/S/full averages from 84.12/82.89/81.22/86.38 to 84.31/82.96/80.86/86.46, while retaining component scores. The introductory separate-critique advantage consequently changes from 5.16 to 5.6 percentage points. These limited revisions preserve the principal rankings.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces termination at Q_t < epsilon with Q_t = 1 or the iteration limit, correcting the inconsistency with Section 3.2's success-indicator definition. The task mapping and agent-update equations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 qualifies the introduction's previously unqualified 11.33% improvement as a comparison against Direct Prompting with Llama 3.2-11B. The central claims about multi-agent generation, test-time scaling, and modality-separated critiques remain; the last is retained in the introduction and conclusion despite leaving the abstract.

C2.justification: The explanations involving modality-specific requirements, context dilution, error propagation, and model-dependent difficulty effects are retained. The limitations concerning prompts, automatic evaluation, computational cost, and the explored scaling range are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain identical verifier code, prompt templates, response limits, API-call accounting, and hardware information. The project-access information is unchanged. Algorithm 1 summarizes the existing procedure without disclosing new implementation settings.

R1.justification: v4 adds Muennighoff et al.'s s1: Simple test-time scaling and introductory context connecting token budgets to reasoning performance. The three related-work strands remain unchanged; Du et al.'s preprint-to-conference update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v4 revises the abstract, reorders introductory motivation, expands the verifier explanation, standardizes several references to accuracy as F1 score or performance, and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds the Algorithm 1 display, relocates Figures 2 and 3, repositions Table 2, and revises several captions. All five figures and both tables retain their basic designs; the appendix layout is preserved.

improvement.justification: v4 improves internal consistency through the numerical revisions in Tables 1–2 and the corrected stopping equation, while clearer F1 terminology and pseudocode aid comprehension. These are useful, limited gains. Remaining inconsistencies include the main text requiring every verification metric to pass a threshold while Appendix A.2 describes thresholding their average.
